## #29 RUN AND READ — THE ENGINE DRAFTS A FIELDABLE, SANELY-SHAPED ROSTER ON A VARIED FIELD

36 arms (6 formats × 6 strategies), 32 effective, 76 findings, 6h43m, at `04bccb5`. Full reading in
`evidence/design_35/RESULT_VDS.md`; the bars were fixed in `PREREGISTRATION_VDS_READING.md` before
either follow-up instrument was built, and the launch gate in `GATE_FOR_VDS.md` before any arm
reported.

**The exercise flag was checked before any number was read**, which is the lesson the previous run
paid for: `weekly_projection_weeks: 18`, `streaming_floor_exercised: true`. `#30` fired on the one
format carrying K and DEF slots.

### What it found

**49 of the 73 `unfieldable_depth` findings are an audit artifact, not engine behaviour.**
`draft_battery._position_of` returns the RAW Sleeper position by deliberate design — its docstring
records this as a latent issue kept unchanged so five committed batteries stay comparable — so a
player whose `fantasy_positions` are `['DL','LB']` counts as an LB while `player_position` buckets
him DL, which is the slot family the optimizer fields him in. Recounted through that bucket, every
flagged HEAVY_IDP roster under a noiseless strategy sits at **LB 3 against a ceiling of 3**. The
audit is left alone for the reason it already states; the recount is committed as
`evidence/design_35/idp_bucket_recount.py`.

**17 of the 24 survivors are the noise model, and that is measured rather than argued.** `noisy_k8`
sets `sharp_seats: []`, so every seat draws uniformly from its own top 8 and no seat is the sharp
engine. `noise_replay.py` reproduces the arm's `pick_sequence` exactly (asserted first) and records
the drawn rank on all 192 picks: all 7 over-ceiling picks came at **rank 5–7 out of candidate lists
of 7–9, in rounds 15–16, and ZERO at rank 0**. The draw is over `min(top_k, len(candidates))`, so
once the list falls below 8 it covers the whole list and reaches the bottom-sorted surplus with
probability 1/7. **That is positive evidence `unfieldable_last` binds:** the only way a surplus body
was taken is a random draw over a list shorter than `k`. In the five non-IDP formats the engine
exceeds no ceiling under any noiseless strategy, and `12T_ppr_SHORT_DRAFT` finished with zero
findings under all six.

### The quality grade, and the one place the bar is missed

Graded on the projected analogue of the realized ruler — each week's best legal lineup under
`lineup_optimizer`, summed over the 18 weeks on disk. **Limit stated, not buried:** both chairs draft
off the same projections, so this measures structure, not forecasting. Value over a best-available
chair is what the 2023/2024 realized work speaks to.

- **vs `raw_bpa` (position-blind): +118 to +496 a seat, 9–12 of 12 seats, all six formats.**
- **vs `sane_bpa` (fills its starting slots first): −10.1 to +23.8 a seat, 5–7 of 12 seats.** The
  pre-registered bar was "ahead in aggregate in every format AND on a majority of seats". **It is not
  met, and it is not being moved after the fact.** The magnitudes are −0.2% to +0.9% of a ~2500-point
  season. The ruler's own resolution, measured from this same run, is ~1%: it separates the engine
  from `raw_bpa` by 118–496 and `sharp_upside` from `sharp_auto` in the same direction in all six
  formats by 20–87. The engine-to-`sane_bpa` gap sits at or under that, so the tie is the ruler
  declining to distinguish two need-aware chairs — the exact limitation `realized_ruler.py` exists to
  escape, whose docstring already measured the projected ruler as INDIFFERENT to the K/DEF placement
  this battery exists to police.
- **Where it separates cleanly, and it is the owner's own question.** Mean players per roster who
  never appear in any week's optimal lineup: `12T_ppr_K_DEF` raw 3.25 / sane 1.67 / **engine 0.50**;
  `HEAVY_IDP` raw 3.75 / sane 1.00 / **engine 0.67**. On the two formats carrying dedicated
  K/DEF/IDP slots the engine wastes a third to a fifth of what `raw_bpa` does and well under half of
  `sane_bpa`'s, at the same or better points — in `12T_ppr_K_DEF`, +0.8 on the ruler with 1.17 fewer
  dead roster spots a team. On the three plain formats it is level or a touch behind.

### TWO THINGS FOR THE OWNER, not repair commits (`#184`)

1. **Upside mode is worse on fieldable value in all six formats.** `sharp_upside` trails `sharp_auto`
   everywhere and `sane_bpa` by 20.8 to 86.6 a seat, ahead on only 2–5 of 12 seats. Same direction,
   six formats, no exceptions. First time the upside-mode gap has been measured on roster quality
   rather than on a board diff.
2. **The `#261` crossing rule is unexercised.** `crossing` reproduced `sharp_balanced` byte-for-byte
   in all six formats, and `picks_with_growth_measured` is **0** for every `crossing` arm — so the
   rule never reached upside mode on a single pick of any of the 36 arms. The battery's own
   `INERT_ARMS` detector cannot see this: it compares each arm to the control only, never pairwise.
   Effective strategy count is 5, not 6.

Neither is a defect the run found in the frozen engine. Both are things the run cannot vouch for,
and the second means a listed axis of this battery covers nothing.

## `#184` DESIGN FINDING — `sharp_upside`'S DIFFERENTIATOR IS INERT, AND THAT IS NOT A PRODUCTION DEFECT

Raised by `#29`, investigated to the arithmetic, ruled by the owner as a post-freeze design item.
Evidence: `evidence/upside_gap/` — `PREREGISTRATION.md` (bars fixed before measuring),
`CHRONOLOGY.md` (order of record, written while M1 was still running), `RESULT.md`, and the four
instruments with their JSON.

**The causal story, measured end to end.** `mode="upside"` discards `need_bonus`,
`eligibility_bonus`, `depth_exposure`, `displacement_adj`, `time_horizon_adj` and `risk_adj` — its own
branch comment says it has "no roster awareness of any kind" — in exchange for
`growth_points = clamp(0.5 × (proj3yr_pct − season_pct), ±10)`. Measured over six pick-1 boards,
6794 rows: `growth_signal > 0` on **200 rows (2.9%)**, tilt ≥ 1 point on **149 (2.2%)**, and the top
row by `final_score` is **the same player as the top row by `bpa` alone in all six formats**. Across
87 real drained states reconstructed from committed arms — `candidates[0]` matching the arm's actual
pick at all 87 — the chosen pick carried positive growth on **2**. A ±10 tilt cannot reorder a board
whose leading rows are tens of points apart.

So the VDS loss of 20.8–86.6 a seat is **the cost of removing the roster-aware terms, not the price
of future value.** M2 closes the alternative: on `proj_3yr`, the vendor quantity the growth term is a
percentile difference OF, `sharp_upside` is behind `sharp_auto` on the best legal 3-year starting
lineup in **all six formats** (−108.6 to −224.6) and on roster total in five of six — 0 of 6 against
a pre-registered bar of "a majority of six". It does not win on the horizon it targets.

**Not a broken implementation.** `upside_score` computes what its docstring says, the `_has_3yr`
guard works (it is what keeps the K/DEF growth artifact out), and the clamp is applied as specified.
No arithmetic defect exists.

**Post-freeze work, stated as work rather than as a fix.** The growth term needs a DERIVED conversion
from percentile difference to points. The ±10 clamp was borrowed from `time_horizon_adj` precisely
because `#56` forbids calibrating a constant, and the borrowing is what makes the term argmax-neutral
— so the answer is a derivation, not a bigger number.

## CARRIED FORWARD — THE UPSIDE BOARD'S FLAT REGION AND ITS `player_id` TIEBREAK

A separate finding from the same investigation, kept separate on the owner's instruction.

**8 of 87 states had the upside board's top candidate tied on value with others; 0 of 87 in balanced
mode at the identical states.** All eight are rounds 12–16 and every tie is at value exactly 0.00,
because the replacement level is a rank SELECTED within the remaining pool, so the player at that
rank prices at exactly zero — and with several positions exhausted, several "best remaining at
position X" rows land on 0.00 together. `player_id` then decides.

**What is tied is not equivalent.** `12T_ppr_K_DEF` R12, 25 candidates, four tied at 0.00: Darnold
QB, Dulcich TE, Mitchell RB, Johnston WR. Balanced mode at the same state values them −41.22, −85.65,
−87.51 and off-board (ranks 21, 22, 23), and takes a **DEF at +1.90** that upside mode does not
surface at all.

**Production cannot reach it.** All three `build_snapshot` call sites in `app.py` omit `mode`; the
`**snapshot_inputs` dict carries no `mode` key; `build_snapshot`'s `"balanced"` default threads into
`compute_draft_board` and into `pick_analysis` → `_build_opponent_boards`, so the rival boards are
balanced too; `detect_positional_run` takes no mode and builds no board; and `app.py` never calls
`roster_diagnostics`. AST-audited over the call sites rather than grepped for the word "upside".

**The `#35` relationship, recorded with both of my wrong turns.** I predicted the tie was created by
`#35`. The first cap-on/cap-off A/B returned an identical board and I called that a refutation — then
the recording wrapper in the same run showed the cap had been **called 13 times and capped nothing**
at that state, making the arm vacuous and the refutation worthless. The eight-state sweep
(`m1d_tie_states_sweep.py`) gives the real relationship: **`#35` does not create the tie** — two
states show a four-way tie with the cap firing on nothing — but where it fires, in 6 of 8 states, it
**enlarges the tie from 2–3 to 4 and changes which player the upside board takes.** None of this
disturbs `#35`, which was certified on realized outcomes on the balanced/auto path production does
use (+21.70 and +43.69 a seat).

**Post-freeze work:** the branch needs a deliberate ordering/tiebreak policy for its flat regions. No
measurement here licenses a replacement, which is why nothing was changed before the freeze.

## #294 — INJURY HISTORY INVESTIGATED AND REJECTED AS A GRADE; `lineup_optimizer`'S REFUSAL TO
## CARRY A BASE RATE IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN MERELY CAUTIOUS

Opened because a league member asked for an injury-probability bar on the draft surface, and the
owner asked whether Sleeper's data could support one. The answer is no. The useful part of that
answer is WHICH hypotheses died and on what evidence, so the next audit does not re-run them.

**Nothing in the engine was changed by this item.** No durability grade, no injury penalty, no
external ingestion, `risk_adj` untouched. It is a recorded negative result plus two corrections.

### The external source that exists, and the two traps inside it

`nflverse-data` publishes per-week NFL roster status (`RES` = injured reserve) and the official
weekly injury report (body part, Out/Doubtful/Questionable), 2009–2025, reachable from this
container and joinable to Sleeper ids. Coverage against the 213-player `ui_explore` fixture board:
169 (79%) via `roster_weekly`'s own `sleeper_id`, 200 (93%) via the `db_playerids` gsis crosswalk.
The 13 unmapped are ALL team defenses — not rookies, which is worth stating because an earlier
reading of this during the session said rookies and was wrong.

**TRAP 1 — the committed Sleeper weekly capture LOOKS like injury history and is not.** Every row
of `sleeper_weekly_2024.json` carries `player.injury_status`, `injury_body_part` and
`injury_start_date`. They are the capture-time record backfilled onto every historical row:
**identical across all 18 weeks for 2,561 of 2,562 players.** The `stats` half of the same row IS
genuine per-week data (`last_modified` moves week to week). A grade built on the `player` half
would describe the capture date while claiming to describe the season.

**TRAP 2 — the official injury report structurally excludes the severe cases.** A player drops off
the weekly report once he is placed on IR. Rashee Rice returns 1 report row and Alex Singleton 0,
against 16 and 15 IR weeks respectively. The join was audited by surname before the data was
blamed — 153 matched, 0 mismatches — so the thinness is the source, not the instrument.
`roster_weekly`'s `RES` status is what captures those absences, and it is also what separates
"hurt" from "did not play": Malik Willis reads ACT 18 / IR 0 while Bradley Chubb reads ACT 0 /
IR 17. `stats.gp` alone cannot make that distinction and ranks Willis as the least available
player on the board.

### The backtest: churn-controlled, per fold, with bootstrap intervals

Offensive skill positions, requiring ≥16 roster weeks in BOTH seasons — the control matters: without
it the first pass returned a BACKWARDS quartile split, an artifact of fringe players being cut and
changing the denominator.

    prior-season IR spell  ->  P(any IR next season), 95% CI
    fold        none                 1-5 wk               6+ wk
    2023->24    0.20 [0.16,0.24]     0.29 [0.17,0.41]     0.25 [0.14,0.36]
                n=408                n=58                 n=56
    2024->25    0.25 [0.21,0.29]     0.33 [0.20,0.46]     0.30 [0.19,0.42]
                n=411                n=46                 n=57

Every injured interval overlaps the none-group mean, and 6+ weeks sits BELOW 1–5 in both folds.

    returned vs not, restricted to onset <= wk13 so both groups COULD return
    fold        returned             never returned
    2023->24    0.27 [0.13,0.40]     0.21 [0.10,0.33]    <- reversed
    2024->25    0.24 [0.11,0.38]     0.32 [0.17,0.46]

    same body part in both seasons
    fold        no IR                IR 6+ wk
    2023->24    0.20                 0.11 [0.04,0.20]
    2024->25    0.14                 0.12 [0.04,0.21]

    age band control, P(any IR next season)
    <=25    no IR 0.20 / 0.23    any IR 0.21 / 0.29      <- no effect
    26-28   no IR 0.20 / 0.27    any IR 0.40 / 0.29      <- folds disagree

### WHAT THIS RULES OUT

- **A severity gradient from IR spell length.** Not monotonic, intervals overlap, and the longest
  spells carry the LOWEST re-IR rate of any injured bucket.
- **"Returning from IR is a positive signal."** The folds disagree in direction once the tautology
  below is removed.
- **Same-body-part recurrence as a usable feature.** Long-IR players show LOWER same-part rates,
  which is detection bias and not protection: a man on IR is off the weekly report, so fewer body
  parts are recorded for him at all and the intersection cannot fire.
- **Blending Out/Doubtful weeks into a PREDICTIVE score.** It roughly halves the association
  (rho +0.422/+0.358 for IR weeks alone against +0.221/+0.203 blended). The blend improves the
  DISPLAY distribution and degrades the prediction; those are different goals and were conflated
  once in this session.

### CORRECTIONS IN FULL

1. **A reported rho of +0.597 for the flag "late IR, never returned" is WITHDRAWN.** It was
   tautological: a week-15 placement cannot return before the season ends, so the flag partly
   re-encodes its own onset term. Restricted to returnable onsets, the effect does not replicate.

2. **"Surface `exposure` — it is already computed and read by nothing" is WITHDRAWN.** Measured on
   the fixture, `depth_basis` is `measured` on **15 of 700 rows**, and by draft state: **early 0 of
   360, mid 0 of 290, late 15 of 50.** Exposure is structurally unavailable during the phase of a
   draft where it would inform a pick — `vacant` before a roster exists, `no_surplus` once it does
   and before a bench does, which `lineup_optimizer` already names as "each starter's own value
   wearing a depth-shaped label", i.e. not depth information. It is also NOT unread: `pick_debate`
   renders it with its basis. The detector's write-only `exposure` is the dict key inside
   `depth_exposure()`'s return, a different object from the scalar on the candidate.

3. **Spearman overstated the effect and the group means are the honest instrument.** The outcome is
   heavily zero-inflated — most players are 0 IR weeks in both seasons — and that mass of
   double-zeros manufactures rank agreement. A rho of +0.42 sits alongside intervals that overlap
   everywhere, and the intervals are what should be believed.

### WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND WHY

- **No base rate is supplied**, which leaves `depth_exposure`'s documented socket open exactly as
  it was: *"A caller that acquires real base rates can weight these numbers; until then they are
  pure severity."* This item is the attempt to acquire them. The result is that they are not
  acquirable at a defensible confidence from three seasons, so the engine's refusal to invent
  "RBs get hurt 1.4x more than WRs" is now backed by measurement rather than only by caution.
- **The negative results are bounded by their own definitions.** Three seasons, two folds that
  share players and are therefore not independent, offensive skill positions only, outcome =
  next-season IR weeks rather than fantasy points lost. They do not establish that no predictive
  injury signal exists in a richer dataset — only that this one does not support a grade.
- **If availability history is ever revisited, `#146` is the precedent to follow, not this item's
  silence.** `bye_week` was ruled admissible in REDRAFT ONLY — "a real cost when you own the player
  for one season and meaningless when the asset outlives the schedule" — gated on
  `league["settings"]["type"]`. A prior-season IR stint has the identical shape.

### What was ALREADY in the record, and was nearly duplicated

Two artifacts were drafted during this investigation and discarded before they were written, because
the register already answers them and a second home is `#126`:

- **A capture protocol to settle the `risk_adj` double-count.** `#191` was RETRACTED AND INVERTED
  already: Sleeper projects injured players for a full season (`gp=17` even on IR), so there is no
  double-count to detect. An independent probe here — weekly projections for Out players at 1.03x
  their own healthy median, 0% zeroed — agrees with it from a different data path, and is recorded
  only as corroboration.
- **A `#172` data-contract finding that `injury_status` is designation-only.** The emitted
  vocabulary table with counts is already printed in the `#191 IR/PUP + #202` entry, measured on
  more rows than this session used.



## #295 — THE PROTOTYPE'S WITHHELD CONTRACT IS NOW ASSERTED, AND ITS REASON SENTENCE HAD A
## SECOND HOME; ONE PUBLISHED CLAIM OF MINE WITHDRAWN

An outside design review of the Doors A prototype raised the withheld survival family: *"a hidden
field in a pretty interface isn't a withheld result. It's a visible result with a curtain over
it."* That is the right question to ask, and the answer here is mixed in a way worth recording,
because two of the three things I first reported were wrong.

### The curtain is real. Measured, not assumed.

`ui_explore/fixture.json` carries `survival_probability`, `opportunity_cost` and
`expected_value_of_waiting` as live numbers on **all 700 candidate rows** — it is the engine
capture, and `capture_fixture.py` takes the family from `ps.withheld_fields()` rather than a
second list. `_build.py` pops them before inlining, so the **built artifacts carry 0 of 700**,
verified by walking every committed `*.html` payload rather than by trusting the build's
docstring. `waiting_cost`, which IS shown, survives: the strip is targeted, not a blanket drop.

So the review's implied present-tense leak was not established, and my own first reading — that
it had caught us — was withdrawn within the same investigation.

### What WAS missing: nothing made it stay true

The strip was one `c.pop(w, None)` in a build script, with no test. `test_withheld_propagation`
audits the four ENGINE surfaces; the prototype is a fifth and was unguarded.
`test_withheld_values_never_reach_the_prototype.py` now holds it, in the shape this repo keeps
re-learning the hard way:

- **The vacuity guard comes first.** An artifact that never carried the fields would pass an
  absence check while proving nothing — the terminology guard whose live population was zero
  could fire and had nothing in range to fire at. So the SOURCE fixture is asserted to carry the
  family as numbers on every row BEFORE the artifact is asserted not to.
- **The walk is schema-agnostic**, over the whole payload rather than a known key path. One
  committed artifact (`_v1_ledger_rail_prev.html`) carries an older schema with no `formats` key,
  which a path-based check would have skipped in silence.
- **`None` is not a leak.** A present key with no value is the absence contract (`#187`) saying
  "asked, does not exist" — a different statement from a suppressed one.
- **Mutation-tested, three arms, each restored**: strip removed from the build → FAILED
  (5 failures); sentence hand-written back → FAILED; fixture stripped of the family → the
  vacuity guard FAILED. Baseline OK before and after.

### THE REAL DEFECT, which the review did not name and my own flag pointed at by accident

`pick_synthesis.WITHHELD_REASON` exists for a stated purpose: *"a hand-copied sentence in each is
four places to go stale the day `SURVIVAL_IS_CALIBRATED` flips."* The prototype had hand-copied a
**fifth**: `"computed, then held back: it failed calibration against real drafts"`.

**WITHDRAWN: my claim that this reason was unsourced.** I grepped `POST_AUDIT_PLAN.md` for the
wording, did not find it, and reported that the UI asserted a cause I could not substantiate. The
cause is fully substantiated — in `survival_is_presentable`'s docstring (*"two arms measured it
losing to a constant predictor"*) with `SURVIVAL_CALIBRATION_EVIDENCE` naming the two evidence
files, both present. I looked in the register for something that correctly lives in the module.
That is the one-home discipline working, and me checking the wrong home.

The hand copy was therefore **accurate and still wrong to exist** — which is precisely the state a
second home occupies before it drifts. And it was already lossy: the engine's sentence also says
the estimate *"is worst exactly where a reader would lean on it hardest"* and *"Do not estimate
one from the numbers that are shown."* The prototype's copy carried neither, so the surface was
understating its own warning. The build now reads `WITHHELD_CARD_TEXT` and `WITHHELD_REASON` from
the engine, verified rendering verbatim in all three withheld rows.

### Two senses of "not charged", separated rather than standardised

The review asked for `"not charged"` to become `"not priced into value"` globally. Globally is
wrong: `lineup_optimizer` uses that phrase of an EXPOSURE figure that is not a depth price
(`EXPOSURE_ROSTER_PARTIAL`, `no_surplus`), and `test_a_roster_the_solver_never_saw_whole` pins it.
The prototype used the same words of an injury DESIGNATION that did not reduce a value. Two
subjects, one wording — and "not charged" can read as a cost assessed and then waived.

So the UI's designation label alone becomes `"not priced into value"`, which also makes the
display agree with the basis key it has always had (`designation_not_priced`). The engine's uses
are untouched. Standardising would have merged two distinct claims; disambiguating separates them.

### A live `undefined` found while reading that code

`KIND` mapped five kinds. The projected-points row sets `k:"not_priced"`, which was **not among
them**, so `KIND[e.k]` was `undefined` and the panel rendered the literal word beside its amber
styling. `shared.css` already had a `.ev.not_priced` rule, so the kind was intended and only its
label was missing. Reachable on 2 of 700 rows (Keyshaun Elliott, LB, `LIGHT_IDP` early and mid —
the only rows with no season projection). Fixed, and verified in the rendered DOM: 16 kind chips,
0 empty or `undefined`.

### Measured and NOT acted on: depth exposure during a draft

The review's closing recommendation was to audit whether `lineup_optimizer.depth_exposure` can be
surfaced in Doors A. It cannot usefully be, and this is the second time that has been measured.
Across the same 700 rows, `depth_basis` is `vacant` on 488, `no_surplus` on 194, `measured` on
**15**, `roster_partially_priced` on 3 — and the 15 are all late-draft (early 0 of 360, mid 0 of
290, late 15 of 50). The cause is structural rather than a wiring gap: exposure prices a DEPTH
loss, which needs a surplus to slide up, and a mid-draft roster has holes instead of surplus.
Where it does exist, `pick_debate` already renders it. No change.

### The suite policed the new guard, on the first full run

Two of this repo's meta-guards failed on the new test file, and both were right:

- `test_prose_names` — the file's own comment said `` `_prev` ``, a backticked name resolving to
  nothing. The rule is "the name exists, or the prose says it is history"; a shorthand for a
  filename is neither. Now `` `_v1_ledger_rail_prev.html` ``.
- `test_suite_taxonomy` — a new test module must cite its audit section or register item in its
  docstring, or it "answers to nothing" and drops out of every coverage query. Now cites `#295`.

Worth recording because it is the same discipline this entry is about, applied one level up: a
guard written to stop an invariant going unstated was itself unstated until the suite said so.


## #296 — `positional_forfeit` MEASURED AGAINST THE BAR ITS COUSIN FAILED; SHOWN WITH ITS LIMIT
## STATED RATHER THAN WITHHELD

The owner asked whether the forfeit carries calibration evidence of its own. It did not, and the
absence was easy to miss because something forfeit-shaped sits in `evidence/`:
`evidence/forfeit_knife_edge/` is a QUANTISATION probe (`#86`, whether `round(expected_taken)` is
a knife-edge), not a calibration. It never asks whether the prediction matched the outcome. So a
number drawn on every door had nothing behind it while its cousin `survival_probability` had been
measured, failed, and withheld everywhere.

### What was measured, and why that quantity

`expected_taken`, not the value terms. `positional_forfeits` walks a position's curve down by
`round(expected_taken)` and reports the drop, so the forfeit is only as good as that count — and
unlike the value terms it is ROSTER-INDEPENDENT. `position_next_turn_value` and the actual best
left at the next turn are not in the same units, because my own roster changes between the two
turns; comparing them would confound the model with my own pick.

**416 (turn, position) pairs, six formats, replayed VDS drafts, turns on the gap AHEAD:**

| predictor | MAE | bias |
|---|---|---|
| model `expected_taken` | 1.459 | **-1.075** |
| per-position constant | **1.388** | 0.000 |
| gap x prior share | **1.365** | 0.000 |
| nothing gets taken | 2.077 | -2.077 |

Beaten by both naive baselines pooled, and by its own per-position constant in 4 of 6 formats.
Reliability off by ~2x and MONOTONIC — a bias, not noise: 0.56 -> 1.32, 1.37 -> 2.60,
2.36 -> 4.68, 3.84 -> 7.33.

### THE CONFOUND RULED OUT, AND THE ONE THAT WAS NOT

Counting the wrong population is the error this repository keeps re-learning, and here it would
have manufactured exactly this bias for free: if `expected_taken` predicts takes from the PRICED
pool only and the instrument counts every body drafted, the model reads low without being wrong.
Both populations are recorded per row. **The restriction is not vacuous** — the priced filter
excludes 489 of 970 rows on an opening `12T_ppr` board — and it changed nothing, because every
intervening pick in every replay was already priced. Identical to three decimals both ways.

NOT ruled out, and stated rather than buried: takes are attributed by `players_db` position, so a
multi-eligible player taken into a flex counts under his listed position. WR carries the largest
bias (-2.04), which is where that would bite hardest. And the replays are engine-driven drafters,
not humans — a limit that cuts both ways, since failing to predict its own kin is not the weaker
indictment.

### RULED: LABEL IT, DO NOT WITHHOLD IT

The direction decides this. Under-counting takes walks the curve down too few players, so the
next-turn value is overstated and the displayed cost of waiting is UNDERSTATED. The door's number
is a floor. That is a conservative aid, which is categorically unlike survival's "62% he lasts" —
a per-player probability a reader leans on directly, and the thing `withheld_fields()` exists for.

So the numbers panel's basis line now states the measured limit, and the figure stays. Withholding
would be the wrong instrument: `#187` holds that a reader shown nothing assumes the data was
missing and reasons around the gap, and this number was already framed as "an aid beside the rank,
never what ranks".

THE DOOR HEADLINE WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. Writing "at least 6.0 less" onto the main surface
would promote one measurement against engine-driven opponents into a claim about every draft. The
limit lives in the panel until someone checks it against human ones.

### `#56` held

This MEASURES. It tunes nothing, and no number here may be written back into the engine as a
constant. The capture's LIMITS forbid calibrating against one league, and that prohibition does
not soften because the error was measured rather than guessed.

Evidence: `evidence/forfeit_calibration/` — `calibrate_forfeit.py` (re-runnable from the repo
root), `forfeit_calibration.json` (every row plus the summary), `RESULT.md`.

## #297 — THE FRONT PAGE'S FIRST REAL COST WAS AN IMPORT, NOT A LAYOUT; AND TWO OF ITS SIX
## CLAIMS CANNOT BE MEASURED FROM A DRAFT AT ALL

The owner asked for a main page, and `ui_explore/round2/MAIN_PAGE.md` argues the shape: a triage
surface answering "what needs you, why, what it costs to ignore, what can wait" — the draft
room's own constraint applied to a week instead of a pick. Building it turned up two things the
design argument could not have known, and both are about what the engine can and cannot say.

### The first cost was `positional_depth`, and it was a scoped piece of `#137`

`positional_depth` — the function behind "thin at TE", and behind the Trade Calculator and the
League Depth Map — lived in `app.py`, which carries 69 top-level Streamlit calls and no
`__main__` guard. Importing it runs the application, so a quantity three surfaces depend on had
no reader outside the app. Two workarounds had grown around that, each documented as one:

- `test_positional_depth_coverage` reached the function by PARSING the UI surface and exec-ing a
  single `FunctionDef` out of it, its own docstring conceding that "the alternative — moving it
  into an importable module — is the hull extraction (`#137`)".
- `depth_value_label` exists as a named top-level function rather than an inline ternary
  *because* that was the only way a test could reach the behaviour at all.

Both moved to `depth_chart.py`, lifted by AST span rather than retyped, so there is no
transcription to audit. The module imports nothing at runtime — the posture `draft_state.py` and
`content_hash.py` take, for the same stated reason. `app.py` imports the two names, so its six
call sites read exactly as before and `test_maintenance_view_wiring`'s anchor is untouched.

**Measured, and the architecture welcomed it:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `app.py` | 7,441 lines | 7,377 |
| `app.py`'s direct `merger.merge_player` reaches | 5 | **4** |
| `boundary_census --check` | 44 allowed, 44 found | "1 fewer than recorded — that is progress" |

`boundary_census` reports shrinkage as progress by design: "a reach going away is the whole point
of the work this file guards." The ceiling was tightened 5 → 4 **in the same change**, because a
ceiling left at the old number is slack the hull can re-widen into without the file saying a
word — the same reason `assertion_floors` is regenerated rather than left high after a real drop.

`test_depth_chart_is_importable` pins what the move bought: the module imports without dragging
in Streamlit or `app` (checked in a SUBPROCESS, because by the time it runs in the full suite
something else has long since imported Streamlit and an in-process check would pass on someone
else's import), `app.py` does not define either name again, and the runtime import list stays
empty. **Mutation-checked 4/1/1/1** — a planted `import streamlit` fires three failures and an
error, a planted `import pandas` one, `app.py` re-defining the function one, `app.py` dropping
the import one — with an unplanted control passing and both files verified byte-identical after.

### What rules OUT: two of the front page's claims cannot be fixtured, and the reason is the same

`compute_readiness` counts `slot == "Starter"`, and `slot` is assigned at `app.py:3792` from
**Sleeper's own `starters` array** — the lineup a human submitted. A drafted roster has players
and no submitted lineup. So "7 of 9 starters set" and the material-injury claim, which the brief
had listed as the cheapest claims on the page because `compute_readiness` is already wired, are
**not measurable from a replayed draft**. Nor is the record: `team_standings` reads
`settings.wins/losses`, and nothing in `data/league_captures/` holds a roster's contents or a
result — those files capture a league's RULES, which is what they were built for.

A fixture generator and a renderer were written to carry that distinction —
`ui_explore/capture_front_fixture.py` stamping every field `measured`, `CONSTRUCTED` or `ABSENT`,
and `ui_explore/round3/build_front.py` drawing a constructed number with its marker and an absent
one as an em dash carrying its reason (`#187`).

**NEITHER IS COMMITTED, BECAUSE THREE ADVERSARIAL PASSES ESTABLISHED THAT BOTH ARE WRONG IN WAYS
THAT PUT FALSE CLAIMS ON SCREEN.** The findings are recorded here because the architecture
argument above survives them and the two implementations do not:

1. **The fixture generator cannot run at all.** `lineup_optimizer.optimize_lineup` requires
   `{"id", "value", "eligible"}` and indexes both directly; the script builds
   `{"id", "name", "position", "team", "bye", "uv"}`. It raises `KeyError: 'eligible'` on the
   first player, so `bye_concentration`, `bye_collision` and `optimize_lineup` are all
   unreachable. `ui_explore/front_fixture.json` does not exist and never did. Eligibility must
   come from `player_universe.player_eligible_positions` rather than the single-bucket
   `player_position`, per MANDATE 2.6 / `#172`.
2. **The claim that "editing the fixture by hand cannot promote a demo value into a
   measurement" is FALSE.** The renderer reads two of five stamps, both only into `title=`
   tooltips, and the footer sentence asserting "thin positions, structural holes and the bye
   profile are measured" is hardcoded prose. Stamping all three `CONSTRUCTED` changes nothing on
   the page. The one failure mode the design claimed to have engineered away is the one that
   produced the artifact under review.
3. **Structural holes are derived from a fail-open free-agent filter.**
   `league_usable_positions` EXPANDS flex slots by design — its docstring says so — so a
   standard league with a FLEX and no dedicated TE slot reports TE as a slot "nobody you own can
   fill, at any price", in crimson, at the top of the page. On empty `roster_positions` it
   returns every known position, which is correct fail-open behaviour for a free-agent filter and
   maximally wrong for a cannot-field-a-lineup claim. `lineup_optimizer.slot_coverage` is the
   function built for the counting question.
4. `(share or 0) * 100` renders a `None` concentration as **"0%"** — a fabricated zero eight
   lines below an `absent()` helper whose docstring reads "Never a zero standing in for one",
   and directly against `bye_concentration`'s "It is None, never 0.0".
5. The single-hole branch interpolates a position code **unescaped** while the multi-hole branch
   escapes it; position codes come from a league capture, so that is injection from upstream data.
6. `BYE_UNKNOWN` renders as the affirmative "no concentrated bye week", and `BYE_PARTIAL` floors
   are announced in the card body while the week strip and the footer contradict them.
7. `depth_value_label` formats with `f"{...:.0f}"` (half-to-EVEN) rather than
   `design_system.figure()` (half-away-from-zero), so a sum landing on 16.5 renders 16 here and
   17 in the Draft Room — the exact two-answers defect `_HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` exists to close,
   reproduced on a new surface. That one belongs in `depth_chart.py`, not the page.

The passes also found the page's routes are `<span>`s at 18.7px rather than links at the 44px tap
floor, the ladder has no concept of the current week (its week-9 claim is about a week already
played), and four text roles use `--dim` at 12px where the design system documents that token as
deliberately below the AA normal-text threshold.

**What IS measured, from a replayed VDS sequence:** thin positions (`positional_depth` +
`depth_ratings.depth_label`, the same judgment the Trade Calculator uses), structural holes, and
the bye profile (`bye_collision` / `bye_concentration` — value lost rather than bodies lost, and
what share of a season's damage lands in one week).

The page's palette is DERIVED, not copied: it calls `design_system.root_css_block()`, the one
place the app's hex values are spelled out. Round 2's prototypes hand-wrote theirs and
`_palette.py` later measured the result — 26 of 27 shared token names visibly different, **none
identical**, including three page grounds a design note had claimed were shared. Numbers go
through `design_system.figure()` so the page cannot become a third answer to a `.5` rounding the
module exists to settle once.

### What is NOT fixed

- **The four questions in `MAIN_PAGE.md` are still the owner's** — the claim-band cap, whether
  "nothing needs you" is an acceptable primary state, whether the phone dock holds views or board
  tools, and how far the palette moves. The page is built to one reading of them, not to a ruling.
- **`HEAVY_IDP/late` still misses the phone scroll budget by 8px**, at 2.01 screens against 2.0.
  The spacing levers `MAIN_PAGE.md` costed reclaimed 21px of genuine slack and closed
  `LIGHT_IDP/late` outright — its entry is GONE from the render gate's known-failure table rather
  than kept, which is the first time that table has shrunk. The last 8px would come out of spacing
  that is no longer slack, and is NOT TAKEN on `#56`'s rule that a bound is not a threshold: 2.0
  screens was authored against an 844px phone screen no browser gives a page, so sizing a change
  to cross 1328px would be fitting it to a number whose own calibration is the open question.

### Corrections, and a suite budget that had gone stale

**The recorded full-suite budget was wrong by 45%.** `close-register-item` carried "3347 tests in
878.3s at `3bb81a7` (2026-09-20)". Measured now, `__pycache__` cleared first per `#240`:
**4235 tests in 1276.5s** — 888 more tests and 398s more wall clock. The skill's own instruction
is to re-measure rather than trust a figure older than the work, and this is why: a `timeout`
sized from the old number would have killed a healthy run at 70% complete.

**Three suite failures are PRE-EXISTING, established rather than assumed.** All three reproduce
identically on a clean `git archive` of HEAD with none of this work present:
`test_version_boundary` ×2 (`'streamlit' not found in {}` — Streamlit is not installed in this
container, so the version recorder has nothing to report) and
`test_data_merger.CompositePoolSizeDampeningTests` (3.3999999999999986 against a 3.0 bound).

**A fourth was mine, and the repo caught it.** `test_prose_names` fires when a backticked name in
prose names something that exists nowhere, and it reported
`{'_load_function': ['test_positional_depth_coverage.py:38']}` — a comment I had just written to
explain what the old loader did, naming the function I had deleted in the same change. Reworded.
That test is the reason this entry describes the loader without backticking it.

## #298 — `python3` ON THIS BOX REACHES 1,059 OF 4,235 TESTS, AND EVERY RATCHET SAYS IT IS FINE

Found while re-checking two of the three "pre-existing failures" `#297` recorded. Both turned out
to be about the environment rather than the code, and chasing the second one surfaced something
larger: **there are two pythons in this container and `python3` resolves to the one that cannot
run this repository.**

### The measurement

Same tree, same minute, 2026-11-04, 238 root test modules:

| interpreter | `-V` | collects | test modules that fail to import | declared requirements present |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/usr/local/bin/python3` | 3.11.17 | **1,059** | **180 of 238** | 1 of 11 |
| `/usr/bin/python3` | 3.13.17 | **4,235** | 0 of 238 | 9 of 11 |

`python3` resolves to the first. The 4,235 figure matches `#297`'s suite exactly, so every
certified number this repository holds — the test count, the 1,276.5s budget — was measured on the
second, which nothing in the procedure said to use.

### Why the broken run does not look broken

`unittest` does not drop a module whose import dies. It substitutes one synthetic
`unittest.loader._FailedTest`, so 180 dead modules report as:

```
Ran 1059 tests ... FAILED (errors=180)
```

`failures=0`. `engine-measurement`'s own shell-hazards section instructs
`grep -n "^FAIL:" -A 25 suite.txt`, and that grep returns **nothing** here. 3,176 test cases that
never ran are reported as 180 lines of a different word, under a summary line whose first number
reads like a healthy suite. This is the `#201` family exactly: not a crash, a plausible number
about something else.

**And both ratchets agree with it.** On 3.11.17, at the same tree:

```
$ python3 assertion_floors.py --check
no guarantee has shrunk (238 modules held to a floor)
exit=0
```

238 modules held to a floor; 180 of them unreachable; exit 0. The floors are not wrong. They are
`ast.parse` over `root.glob(TEST_GLOB)` — they answer a question about the SOURCE TREE, and
reachability is a different question that nothing was asking. Same shape as
`ui_explore/round2/fableA/_domdiff.py` hashing markup and therefore being blind to CSS: a
boundary, not a bug, and one that had never been written down.

### What it rules out

* **Not a `PATH` accident in one shell.** The suite task, the app launch and the interactive
  shells all resolve `python3` the same way; the app only worked because `pip3`'s shebang is
  `#!/usr/bin/python3`, so the install landed on 3.13 and `streamlit run` found it there.
* **Not the missing provider SDKs.** `anthropic` and `openai` are absent from 3.13 too, and cost
  **zero** tests: no test module imports either, and every provider call in the suite is stubbed
  (`test_version_boundary`'s own comment says so). The 2 missing distributions under the good
  interpreter are genuinely free.
* **Not `streamlit` being imported by the suite.** Measured: after importing all 238 test modules
  under 3.13, `'streamlit' in sys.modules` is **False**. No test module imports it at module
  scope. Its absence cost exactly 2 tests, both of which only read its *metadata* — see the
  correction below.
* **Not `dotenv` being stubbed by a sibling module.** An early hypothesis here was that
  `test_version_boundary` only imports during discovery because something else puts `dotenv` in
  `sys.modules` first. Wrong, and simpler than that: `dotenv` is installed under 3.13 and absent
  under 3.11, and the standalone run that failed was simply on the wrong interpreter. Recorded
  because the wrong explanation was the more interesting one and would have sent the next reader
  looking for stub machinery that does not exist.

### CORRECTION to `#297` — two of its three "pre-existing failures" were the environment

`#297` recorded "suite 4235 tests, 3 pre-existing failures". That count stands; its composition
does not. Measured after this session installed `streamlit` 1.66.1 into 3.13:

```
$ /usr/bin/python3 -m unittest test_version_boundary
Ran 26 tests ... OK
```

* `test_an_installed_distribution_reports_its_real_version` — **was** `[] != ['streamlit']`
* `test_a_partially_reporting_environment_still_records_what_it_can` — **was**
  `'streamlit' not found in {}`

Both now pass. Neither was ever a code defect: both patch `_PROVIDER_SDK_DISTRIBUTIONS` to
`("streamlit",)` and read `importlib.metadata.version`, on the premise stated in the test's own
comment — *"streamlit is a hard dependency of this app and is installed wherever the suite
runs."* **That premise was false in this container**, and the test was right to say so. It is the
only instrument in the repository that noticed, and it noticed by accident, from one layer down.

So the honest restatement is: **one** code-level failure, `test_data_merger`'s stale `3.0` bound
(still open, still the owner's ruling — `#56`: the behaviour matches the test's prose and the
constant does not), plus two environment artifacts now resolved.

### The guard: `suite_reach.py`

Every module in `assertion_floors.TEST_GLOB`'s population must be importable, zero tolerance. Two
design decisions are the whole value:

1. **The expectation is DERIVED, not recorded.** No floor file, nothing to regenerate, nothing to
   go stale. A new test module raises the population and asks nothing of anybody. The glob is
   *imported* from `assertion_floors` rather than restated, and `test_suite_reach` asserts
   `assertIs`, not `assertEqual`, so a second spelling of `test_*.py` fails the suite (`#126`).
2. **It imports nothing that needs a declared requirement**, so it survives — and fails loudly
   under — precisely the interpreter it exists to detect. A check that dies with the thing it is
   checking is not a check. On 3.11 it answers in 0.54s with the cause (`No module named
   'pandas'`) and the interpreter, rather than 180 buried `ERROR:` lines.

The collected-case count is **reported and never asserted on**. It is the figure a reader wants,
and it also moves every time anyone writes a test, so holding it to a floor would be the
reflexive-repair trap `assertion_floors`' own docstring rejects.

**A defect found in the guard before it shipped, recorded because the repo keeps finding this
class:** the first draft globbed `root` and then resolved imports against `sys.path`, so every
`root` except `.` silently answered about a different population than the one it had just listed.
A parameter half-honoured is worse than one not offered, because the caller is told it was read.
Caught by writing the test that passes a temporary directory — not by reading the diff.

Mutation-checked, 7 arms, all caught: glob restated locally `1`; root never put on `sys.path`
`5`; `except BaseException` narrowed to `except Exception` `1`; `_FailedTest` filter removed `1`;
`report` re-measuring instead of rendering what it was handed `1`; `--check` always succeeding
`1`; root left on `sys.path` `1`. Baseline and restored both green.

### What is NOT fixed

* **The missing requirements are not installed into 3.11, deliberately.** The fix belongs in the
  environment's setup script (`cd The-Dynasty-Collective && pip install -r requirements.txt`),
  which is the owner's to change and outlives the container; this session's `pip install` does
  not. Installing them here would also mask the finding rather than guard it, and the guard is
  the durable half.
* **`close-register-item` now derives the interpreter rather than naming one.** A path with
  `3.13` in it would be the `ui-authority-pass` mistake in a new costume — that skill already
  carries the scar of a hardcoded name going stale. `engine-measurement` points at it and
  restates nothing (`#126`).

## #299 — SIXTEEN BOARD-EXECUTING TESTS HAD BEEN SKIPPING, AND `requirements.txt` HAD WARNED ABOUT IT IN PROSE

Found immediately after `#298`, hunting the suite's 17 skips. The same family — a count nobody
holds to a floor — with a different cause and a complete fix.

### The measurement

This container provisions `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`. The two test
modules that EXECUTE the board looked for it like this:

| file | what it looked for | result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_216_room_integrity.py` | `glob("/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-*/chrome-linux/chrome")` | missed by the `64` |
| `test_board_renders_absence.py` | `CHROME = "/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome"` | missed by the `64` **and** by 49 builds |

Both gates therefore read "no browser here":

```
test_216_room_integrity        12 run, 10 skipped  ->  22 run, 0 skipped, OK
test_board_renders_absence      2 run,  6 skipped  ->   8 run, 0 skipped, OK
```

**All 16 pass.** The board renders correctly and always did; the tests that prove it were not
running. 16 of the suite's 17 skips were this.

### The lesson had already been learned ten feet away

`ui_explore/round2/fableA/_shoot.py:320` carries this comment, in the repository, today:

> `chrome-linux/chrome` on one and `chrome-linux64/chrome` on another, and a glob knowing only
> [one] …

and globs `chrome-linux*/chrome` accordingly. `_domdiff.py` and `_converge.py` learned it too.
**The knowledge never reached the two files where it gated tests** — which is the argument for
`#126` stated as a measurement rather than a principle: the same fact lived in eight files, three
of them had the current version of it, and the two that mattered most had the oldest.

`requirements.txt` also already warned, in its `playwright` comment: *"a reclaimed container ran
the suite 14 tests lighter and reported OK. A freeze must be licensed by a suite that ran, not
one that quietly stood down."* That warning was live, pointed at the right thing, and nobody was
looking — because **a skip is not a failure**, and the number it moves is the one number in the
summary line that no ratchet holds.

### `browser_binary.py` — one home, and three things no scattered copy had

* **Both directory layouts** (`chrome-linux*`), which is the part `_shoot.py` knew.
* **The stable symlink first.** `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` points at the real binary and survives
  a version bump; trying it first makes the version sort a fallback rather than the mechanism.
* **Version suffixes sort NUMERICALLY.** Every copy in this repo reached for
  `sorted(glob(...))[-1]`, which is right for `chromium-1194` vs `chromium-1243` and wrong the
  moment a three-digit build appears: `"1243" < "999"`, so lexical `[-1]` picks build 999 over
  build 1243. No copy had hit it yet. Cheaper to fix than to wait for.
* **`headless_shell` ranked below a full `chrome`, never substituted silently** — it is a
  different product, not another spelling.
* **Returns `None`, never a path that will fail later** (`#187`), because callers differ: a test
  module wants to skip with a named reason, a render gate wants to die loudly. `why_not()` gives
  either one a sentence that names the four places searched, and names `requirements.txt` as the
  authority on not running `playwright install` to "fix" it.

Wired into the two test modules and the three `ui_explore` scripts that were broken by the same
stale glob (`fableA/_interact.py`, `fableB/_shot.py`, `fableB/_interact.py` — each would have
raised `IndexError` on an empty glob today). Removing the inline lookup also retired
`test_216_room_integrity`'s now-unused `glob` and `shutil` imports.

### What is NOT fixed, and why

`_shoot.py`, `_domdiff.py` and `_converge.py` still carry their own copy of the lookup. They are
**correct today** — they are the ones that had the current knowledge — and they are the certified
render gate: `#297`-era certification rests on a 397-render run through `_shoot.py`, and changing
how it finds its browser means re-running that gate to re-license it. Deferred on purpose, named
here so it is a decision and not an oversight. Unifying those three is the follow-up; it should be
done in a commit whose only content is that change, with the gate re-run beside it.

### A process failure in this session, recorded rather than tidied away

The first full-suite run for `#298` was launched and then **voided by my own edits while it ran.**
Python imports test modules once at discovery, so editing them mid-run does not change what
executes — but this repository is full of tests that read SOURCE FROM DISK at runtime
(`assertion_floors`, `prose_names`, `ui_source`, `boundary_census`, and several that `open()` a
module and parse it). Those tests saw a tree that existed at no commit. The run was killed by PID
and discarded, and the certification below is a clean run on the final tree.

This is the second time this shape has cost a run in this session — the first was rebuilding a
prototype mid-gate, which is what `_gatelock.py` and the immutable snapshot were built for. The
gate learned it; the suite had not. **The suite has no equivalent of `_gatelock`**, and that is
now a known gap rather than a surprise: nothing stops a session from editing the tree under a
running `unittest discover`, and nothing in the output would say it happened.

### And a SECOND process finding, which is the more useful one: the git INDEX is part of the tree

The clean re-run was voided too, by something that is not an edit at all. Nine test modules
reach for `git ls-files` rather than globbing the filesystem:

```
prose_names.py   doc_index.py   test_doc_index.py   test_ordinal_registers.py
test_superseded_proposals.py   + test_denial_basis, test_engine_baseline,
test_instruments_check_rather_than_count, test_threshold_reachability,
test_the_four_undefended_repairs (all via the first two)
```

Two consequences, and neither was written down anywhere:

1. **A new module's prose is UNCHECKED until it is staged.** `suite_reach.py`, `browser_binary.py`
   and `test_suite_reach.py` sat untracked through an entire full-suite run, and
   `test_prose_names` reported OK without reading one line of them. `assertion_floors` did see
   `test_suite_reach.py` -- it globs the filesystem -- so the two instruments disagreed about
   whether the file existed, and only the stricter-looking one was blind.
2. **`git add` is therefore a change the suite can observe**, with no file modified. Staging
   mid-run changed what those nine modules measured, which voided the run as surely as editing
   a source file would have.

And the check earned its keep immediately. Staging first, then re-running those nine:

```
test_prose_names   FAILED (failures=1)
AssertionError: {'KeyboardInterrupt': ['suite_reach.py:93']} != {}
```

A builtin, backticked in a docstring I had just written, in a file the full suite had already
passed over. `test_prose_names` holds backticked names to things that exist in THIS repository,
which is the correct rule and one I had walked straight into -- the sibling name in the same
sentence survived only because `test_suite_reach.py` happens to carry it as a string literal,
which that module's own docstring says lands in the haystack. Reworded, and the reason is now
written into the sentence so the next reader does not reintroduce it.

**So the order in `close-register-item` was wrong, and is now fixed.** Staging was step 6, beside
the commit. It has to come BEFORE step 4, because nine of the checks step 4 runs cannot see an
unstaged file:

    git add -A  ->  read git status --short  ->  FULL SUITE  ->  commit

This does not relax the staging rules that section already carries -- never name files, never
silence `git add`, read `git status --short` rather than trusting an exit code. It moves them
earlier, which is also where they do the most good: a broken commit caught before a 21-minute
run costs nothing.

## #299 CORRECTED — IT WAS 15 SKIPS, NOT 16, AND THE WRONG NUMBER CAME FROM MY OWN INSTRUMENT

`#299` above states "**16 board-EXECUTING tests** had been skipping" and "16 of the suite's 17
skips were this", and the table reports `test_216_room_integrity` going from "12 run, 10 skipped"
to 22. **The measured answer is 15, and 13 run / 9 skipped.** Commit `96bb4a8` carries the wrong
figure in both its register entry and its commit message; this entry is the correction, published
rather than edited in place.

### What the certification run actually says

Clean full suite at `96bb4a8`, `/usr/bin/python3` 3.13.17, `__pycache__` cleared first per
`#240`:

```
Ran 4248 tests in 1682.734s
FAILED (failures=1, skipped=2, expected failures=1)      errors=0
```

The baseline runs either side of `#297` both reported `skipped=17`. 17 - 2 = **15 recovered**.

### Where the 16 came from, which is the same failure this whole pass is about

The 16 was never measured. It was COUNTED, by an AST pass I wrote to total the tests behind a
browser gate, and that pass made two errors that nearly cancelled:

| | effect |
|---|---|
| treated **every** `skipUnless` as the browser gate | wrongly included the 2 tests behind `skipUnless(CAPTURE.exists())` at `test_216_room_integrity.py:435` — a different gate, on a condition that is TRUE here, so those 2 were never skipping |
| looked only at DECORATORS | missed the runtime gate at `:455`, where `test_python_and_the_browser_round_the_boundary_class_identically` calls `self.skipTest` from inside the method body after testing the same condition |

8 genuinely decorator-gated + 2 wrongly included = 10. 8 + 1 runtime = **9**, the truth. The two
errors differed by one, so the total looked plausible and sat one away from correct — which is
precisely why it survived being written into a register entry and a commit message.

**A decorator census is not a skip measurement.** I used one as the other.

### The measurement that should have been taken first

Patching `find_chromium` to return `None` before the test module is imported reproduces the
stale glob's exact effect, because the skip decision is made at class-decoration time:

```
test_216_room_integrity:     ran 22, skipped 9  (9 on the browser, 0 on anything else)
test_board_renders_absence:  ran  8, skipped 6  (6 on the browser, 0 on anything else)
```

9 + 6 = 15, matching 17 -> 2 exactly. So the corrected table for `#299` is:

| module | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_216_room_integrity` | 13 run, **9** skipped | 22 run, 0 skipped, OK |
| `test_board_renders_absence` | 2 run, 6 skipped | 8 run, 0 skipped, OK |

Everything else in `#299` stands: all 15 pass, the board renders correctly and always did, the
stale glob and the hardcoded build 1194 were both real, and `browser_binary.py` is the fix.

### What the certification confirms, and the one failure left

* **`errors=0`** — every one of the 239 test modules imported, which is `#298`'s guard reporting
  from inside the suite rather than from a preflight.
* **`failures=1`** — `test_data_merger.CompositePoolSizeDampeningTests`, `3.3999999999999986 not
  less than 3.0`. `#297`'s two `test_version_boundary` failures are GONE, confirming they were
  the absent `streamlit` and not code. One code-level failure remains, and it remains the
  owner's ruling: the behaviour matches the test's prose (a 3.40 move on a 37.5 half-gap is
  9.1% of it) and the hardcoded `3.0` does not. `#56` — a bound is not a threshold.
* **The budget moved and is re-dated in `close-register-item`**: **4248 tests in 1682.734s** at
  `96bb4a8` (2026-11-04), against **4235 in 1276.5s** at `dbae709` the same day. 13 more tests,
  406s slower, 32%. The 15 recovered tests each launch Chromium and are part of it; measured
  standalone those two modules cost 30.2s and 1.8s, which does NOT account for 406s, so the rest
  is unattributed and is not claimed. Budget from the total, as that file already says.

### The 2 remaining skips, named — and the distinction that makes them fine

Measured by running all 26 modules that carry a skip gate, individually:

| module | why it skips |
|---|---|
| `test_draft_room` | "no max-positive-trajectory player in the current real pool is also thin-bpa and non-negative while healthy" — and the message goes on to print the best candidate's `bpa` against the computed thin bound, so a reader can see HOW FAR the real pool was from the condition |
| `test_kdst_integration` | "no contested row is in the projection-only slice on this baseline" |

Per-module total: **2**. Suite total: **2**. They agree, so neither skip is ordering-dependent —
worth checking rather than assuming, because a skip that only fires in full-suite context would
mean the per-module number could never be trusted again.

**And this is the distinction `#299` was really about, which nothing had stated:**

* A skip whose reason names a **DATA CONDITION** is informative. The real pool genuinely contains
  no instance of the case, the test declines rather than fabricating one, and the message carries
  the measurement that proves it. That is the absence contract (`#187`) applied to coverage: the
  test says "not measured, and here is why" instead of inventing a fixture that would make the
  assertion vacuous. Both survivors are this kind.
* A skip whose reason names **MISSING INFRASTRUCTURE** is a silent coverage loss. Nothing about
  the subject under test changed; the harness simply could not reach it. The 15 browser skips
  were this kind, and they are indistinguishable from the first kind in the summary line, which
  is the entire reason they sat unnoticed through an unknown number of runs.

The summary line gives one number for both kinds. `skipped=17` was 15 of the second kind and 2
of the first, and no instrument in the repository could tell them apart. `browser_binary.why_not()`
is a small step against a recurrence — a skip reason that names the four places searched reads as
infrastructure rather than as data — but the general case is open and is NOT fixed here: nothing
classifies a skip, and nothing holds a floor under the count of either kind.

## #300 — THE FRESHNESS MANIFEST LEAVES THE HULL, AND A TEST THAT PREDICTED ITS OWN BREAKAGE WAS RIGHT

A scoped piece of `#137`, chosen because it is the one thing the front page needs that the app can
honestly show with no league synced.

### Why this function

`app.py` called `build_freshness_manifest(st.session_state.league_snapshot or {}, merger)`. The
`or {}` is deliberate — the comment beside it says the grade is *"informational only, not a
gate"*, and the caption under it says *"nothing here blocks the app"*. So the Data Freshness grade
is the one real claim available in the empty state, which `#299`-adjacent work established is the
state the front page exists to replace: `app.py` has exactly ONE `st.stop()`, at 3667, and
everything below it — the five-option view picker included — is unreachable until a league exists.

A front-page fixture could not compute it, because reaching it meant importing a module whose
import runs `st.set_page_config`.

### What moved, and what it cost

Verbatim, by AST span — not retyped. Every comment moved with it (`#140` on the calendar-date
boundary, `#118` on the players database, MANDATE 2.1(c) on the season sums), because each records
a measurement that is the reason a line exists. `recency_grade` already lived in `data_merger` and
is not duplicated.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `app.py` | 7,377 lines | 7,337 |
| `boundary_census` | **43** reaches (ceiling 43) | **41** (ceiling tightened to 41) |

The two reaches that left are `sleeper_client.players_freshness_entry` and
`sleeper_client.season_projection_freshness_entry`. Both are **delisted** rather than set to 0 —
an entry at 0 asserts "this reach is expected to be absent", and nothing in that file wants to
claim that about a function it no longer knows. The ceiling tightens in the same commit as the
removal, which is the precedent the `#297` comment in that file already set.

Measured, in a subprocess, because this process's own `sys.modules` would decide the answer:
importing `freshness` pulls in `league_config`, `player_universe`, `sleeper_client`, `store_io` —
and **not** `streamlit`, **not** `app`, **not** `pandas`, and **not** `data_merger`. The last one
is the `TYPE_CHECKING` guard working: `DataMerger` is needed for the signature and nothing else.

### A TEST PREDICTED THIS EXACT BREAKAGE, IN WRITING, AND IT PAID OFF

`test_sleeper_client.TheManifestActuallyAppendsThePlayersRowTests` read the manifest's SOURCE
through `ui_source` rather than off `app.py`, and said why:

> "the manifest is a candidate for #137's hull extraction, and a raw app.py read would stop
> covering it the moment the view moves — silently, with the test still green."

The extraction happened. `ui_source` searches only modules with a top-level `import streamlit`,
and the entire point of this move is that freshness is NOT UI — so the read did not follow the
function. **It failed loudly**, with `no UI module contains 'def build_freshness_manifest' --
searched app.py`. That is precisely what choosing `ui_source` over a raw read bought, and it is
worth recording as an instrument working rather than as breakage.

The repair goes one better than restoring the read. The function is now IMPORTABLE, which it was
not before, so both guarantees are asserted BEHAVIOURALLY:

* "the players row reaches the manifest" → call it and look for the row.
* "appended before the sort" → assert an UNDATED row sorts **last**, which is the property the
  source-order check was a proxy for. Its own docstring said so: an absent cache's `None` row
  landing at the top is "the exact opposite of what that column asks for."

A behavioural assertion cannot go silently green when the function moves again, from anywhere to
anywhere. That is strictly stronger than what the docstring was reaching for.

### The ratchet fired, as designed

```
A guarantee got smaller.
  test_sleeper_client.py: self.assertLess 1 -> 0
  test_sleeper_client.py: test method ...test_build_freshness_manifest_appends_the_players_entry is gone
  test_sleeper_client.py: test method ...test_the_entry_is_appended_before_the_sort_that_orders_it is gone
```

This is the SUBSTITUTION case `assertion_floors`' own docstring describes — it cannot tell a
weakening from a strengthening, so it fails either way and asks a human to look. Looked at: the
`assertLess` was `body.index(a) < body.index(b)` over source text, and it is gone because the
thing it indexed is gone. The two methods were renamed when they became behavioural. Coverage went
UP — 2 source-reading tests became 2 behavioural ones, plus 11 new in `test_freshness.py`.
Regenerated in this same commit so the drop is reviewable rather than incidental.

Removing the lookup also retired `test_sleeper_client`'s now-unused `import ui_source`.

### Mutation-checked, 7 arms — and one of them was MY ARM that was wrong, not the coverage

Counts, all caught: `DataMerger` imported at runtime `1`; a top-level `import streamlit` added
`1`; the unconditional players row dropped `8`; the sort removed `2`; **the sort moved before the
unconditional appends `2`**; the league sync row made unconditional `11`; the days column changed
to elapsed hours `1`. Baseline and restored both green.

The fifth arm — the `#118` defect itself, the one that matters most — reported **NOT CAUGHT** on
its first run, which read as my behavioural replacement being weaker than the source-order test it
replaced. It was not. **The arm was built wrong**: it inserted a sort before the appends while
leaving the real sort at the end, so the list was still sorted correctly and the mutation was a
no-op. Rebuilt to genuinely MOVE the sort — remove it from the end, place it before both appends —
it fires on 2 tests.

Recorded because the first reading was the alarming one and the instinct it produced was wrong.
A mutation arm is an instrument too, and `engine-measurement`'s rule applies to it unchanged: when
ON and OFF look identical, find out why before concluding.

### What is NOT done

The front page itself is not built. This removes the stated blocker — the content is now reachable
without Streamlit — but the empty-state page is a design question, and the four questions in
`ui_explore/round2/MAIN_PAGE.md` are still open for the owner. What `#300` establishes is that
when those are answered, the answer does not require importing the app to render a date.

## #301 — THE PAGE THE APP ACTUALLY SHOWS TODAY, BUILT FROM MEASURED DATA

`#300` established that the freshness manifest is reachable without Streamlit. This builds the
page that needs it.

### Why it is a second page and not the first one with holes in it

`app.py` has exactly ONE `st.stop()`, at 3667, guarded by `if not snapshot`. The five-option view
picker (3742) and all five view branches sit BELOW it. So with no league synced, none of the
synced front page's claims — lineup holes, bye damage, thin positions — has a SUBJECT to be
about. Rendering them with absent stamps would be a dashboard of em dashes, and that is `#187`
used as an excuse rather than honoured: the absence contract is for a quantity that could not be
measured, not for one that does not yet have anything to measure.

### What the page says, measured on this machine

```
       71d  2026-08-25   Draft Sharks Dynasty Rankings
       76d  2026-08-20   Draft Sharks Trade Value Chart
         -  -            Sleeper player database            never fetched on this machine
         -  -            Sleeper season projections         never fetched

recency_grade(76) = 'Aging'
```

Four bands, nothing more: **is this ready** (the grade and the oldest age), **on disk now**,
**arrives when you sync**, **do this** (the one action, with its cost — until a sync the board
cannot price to the league's rules, because the player universe and the league-scored projections
both arrive with it).

### THE SPLIT IS THE DESIGN, and it is the one thing these tests really guard

Two of the four rows are undated, and they do NOT mean what the two dated ones mean. Before a
sync, "never fetched on this machine" is the EXPECTED state of a machine with no league. After
one it would be damage. A page that renders them identically in both states is lying in one of
them, so the fixture sorts them into `have` and `on_sync` keyed on the STATE, and the renderer
never has to guess.

The stamp stays `ABSENT -- <reason>` either way. The framing comes from the section heading, not
from corrupting the basis.

### Three defects the real browser found that reading the source did not

1. **`no_league_synced` was on the page.** A machine identifier, visible to a person.
2. **The pending rows said "absent" twice** — once as a `.prov` stamp and once by implication from
   the heading — which made an early state read as a broken one. `_row` now takes `stamp=None` to
   mean "the heading already said what these are".
3. **The reason was hover-only.** `absent()` renders an em dash with its reason in `title=`, which
   is right when a NUMBER is missing: the dash stands in for the figure and the tooltip explains.
   These rows have no number missing — the measurement has not been taken — so the reason is the
   content, and it is now visible text. That also removed two 18px focusable spans that the tap
   floor flags.

Rendered after the fixes, both viewports: **0 console errors, no horizontal scroll, 1.0 screens,
min font 12px, no literal `None`/`NaN`/`undefined`, nothing under the 44px tap floor.**

### One stylesheet for both states, and the measurement that demands it

`build_front.style_css()` is lifted verbatim out of `build`'s own f-string and imported by
`build_empty`. Not aesthetics: `_palette.py` compared the round-2 prototypes against the app and
found **26 of 27 shared token names carrying a visibly different colour, with NOT ONE identical**,
including three page grounds a design note had claimed were shared. Two STATES of one page
defining `.fact` and `.claim` separately would drift exactly that way, invisibly, until someone
put the screenshots side by side.

**The lift is verified byte-identical.** `front.html`'s sha256 before and after is
`7e485f83ba63fb956802b26045ffc125af8089ef7971d8e6c88a985b93e3e3ff`, and the build was confirmed
deterministic first (a rebuild of the untouched tree reproduced the committed file exactly), which
is the only reason refactoring a certified file is safe to do at all. Its 18 tests still pass.

### Mutation-checked, 7 arms, all caught

Reason hidden in a tooltip again `1`; pending rows stamped again `1`; the grade hardcoded `1`;
`worst_days` stringified instead of going through `ds.figure` `3`; the raw state key back on the
page `1`; a second stylesheet instead of the shared one `2`; the label no longer escaped `1`.

**The fourth arm survived its first run, and that one was a real gap, not a bad arm.** With the
fixture's `worst_days = 76`, `ds.figure(76, 0)` and `str(76)` both give `"76"` — the mutation is
invisible for the only input the tests used. Measured where they diverge rather than guessing:
`ds.figure(76.5, 0)` is `"77"` against `"76.5"`, and NaN/inf return `None` (so the caller picks
the wording) against the machine words `"nan"`/`"inf"`. Two tests added for exactly those, and the
arm now fires on three. A test that only exercises the input where two functions AGREE proves
nothing about which one ran.

## #303 — EVERY PLACE THE SUITE MAY DECLINE IS NOW REGISTERED

`#299` ended by naming a gap and not closing it: `skipped=17` meant 15 of MISSING INFRASTRUCTURE
and 2 of a DATA CONDITION, nothing could tell them apart, and no instrument held either count.

`skip_gates.py` registers **46 gates across 26 modules**. Growth is the regression; shrinkage is
free. The fix for a legitimate new gate is to register it with a reason, which is the bargain
`boundary_census` already strikes — and it converts a skip gate from something that appears in a
diff nobody reads into something that cannot appear without a sentence explaining itself.

**Why it counts GATES and not SKIPS, stated because the obvious design is the other one.** A
runtime skip count needs a 28-minute suite to measure, so the recorded number could only be
refreshed at enormous cost; and it is environment-dependent by nature, so a developer without a
browser would fail the ratchet for something that is not a code change. The set of PLACES a skip
can happen is static, cheap and environment-independent.

**What it cannot see, and this is the honest limit: whether a registered gate FIRES.** An
always-true gate and an always-false one look identical here. `#299`'s was always-false for an
unknown period and this file would NOT have said so. It would only have required that the gate be
registered in the first place — a weaker and much cheaper guarantee than the one a reader might
assume from the name.

Mutation-checked, 8 arms, all caught: `skipTest` dropped from the vocabulary `2`; `skipIf`
dropped `2`; a wholly new module's gates ignored `2`; shrinkage reported as a problem `1`; a
damaged registry raising `1`; `TEST_GLOB` restated locally `1`; zero-gate modules recorded `2`;
the line number dropped `1`.

**The fourth arm survived its first run — another real gap.** The test removed a module's LAST
gate, which makes `scan()` omit the module entirely, so the comparison never visits it and `!=`
looks identical to `>`. The direction only shows when a module stays present with a SMALLER
number. A 2-gates-to-1 test was added and the arm fires.
